audits.general_notes:
1. Security Gate 2: Odometer reading and fuel level are not being recorded at vehicle entry.
2. Vehicle Updates & Documentation: Service Advisors are not capturing all mandatory photographs in the M Tab. WhatsApp updates regarding vehicle receipt, work in progress, changes or delays in delivery time, vehicle readiness, and pending jobs are not being consistently shared.
3. Repeat Repairs: Repeat repair cases are not being recorded, affecting traceability and corrective action monitoring.

Major observations:

Vehicle receiving: Odometer/fuel recording and proper damage marking were not maintained.
Customer communication: Delivery timelines and WIP/vehicle-ready updates were not consistently documented.
Road Test & Diagnosis: Road-test records showed repetitive/copy-pasted observations, with inadequate evidence of post-repair verification.
Final QC: QC was being handled by the Service Advisor, FI records were not updated, and no adequate repeat-repair/QC documentation was available.
Billing: Labour/parts relevance issues were identified in two JCs, including “Engine Cover Dirty” with unrelated parts and “Noise from Front” with ZA50L0 – All Electricals Check-up.
Discount control: Approx. 20% discount approved by AWM Mr. Pankaj was not reflected in the discount sheet submitted to Accounts

audits.general_notes:
Security Gate: Security gate was found loose, indicating inadequate control over vehicle movement and workshop security.
Diagnosis & Observations: Diagnosis findings and observations were not being recorded properly on the job cards.
Process Discipline: The facility is an authorized Maruti after-sales workshop and not a local garage; therefore, prescribed processes, documentation and quality controls are expected to be followed rigorously.
DLR / Microfibre Cloth: Microfibre cloths were being issued frequently as DLR, raising concerns regarding proper justification and control of such consumables.
Paint Consumption: No record/register for paint consumption was available for verification.
Road Test Compliance: Road test records raised doubts regarding whether the road tests were actually being conducted as recorded. The job sheet and road test register were not matching.
Road Test Duration: Road tests of as little as 3 minutes were recorded, raising questions regarding the adequacy and effectiveness of the road test.
TA Findings: No findings/observations were recorded by the Technician/TA following the road test, weakening the traceability and verification of the activity.
Overall Concern: The above observations indicate gaps in process adherence, documentation, accountability and control, which require immediate corrective action.

audits.general_notes:
Customer communication is largely being handled through calls rather than documented WhatsApp/SMS communication.
Previous pending jobs, delivery timelines and additional work approvals are not consistently documented.
Parts controls are weak, including advance billing, multiple signatures, lack of traceability and inadequate replaced-parts handling.
Road test and final QC processes are not adequately documented or followed.
Billing/payment controls require attention, including advance billing, an undeposited customer payment, advisor signing on behalf of the customer and dealer absorption issues.
Vehicle delivery documentation and customer acknowledgement processes are weak.
Warranty documentation, parts transfer records and technical escalation records were not adequately available.
Paint booth/paint consumption controls require strengthening, including proper manpower, register and stock/reconciliation controls.

Overall conclusion: The audit indicates significant gaps in process adherence, documentation, customer communication, parts/billing controls and supervisory discipline, despite several basic operational and safety areas being compliant.

audits.general_notes:
The TP Nagar audit indicates multiple process gaps in day-to-day operations and compliance. While staff are generally aware of the prescribed SOPs, negligence and lack of consistent supervision were observed in their implementation.

Key observations include:

Staff are not adequately sensitized towards consistent adherence to defined processes and SOPs.
Required WhatsApp communication groups have largely not been formed, resulting in gaps in timely communication and coordination.
Communication gaps between customers and Service Advisors were observed, particularly in relation to process/status communication.
Cleaning activities are not being adequately supervised, indicating a gap in monitoring and accountability.
Tab usage at the security gate was not observed, indicating non-adherence to the prescribed security process.
Paint consumption is being recorded manually; however, in the absence of a standardized RO-wise consumption and variance monitoring mechanism, it is difficult to establish actual paint utilization, identify abnormal consumption/wastage and monitor repeat deviations.
